verdict.rationale: Community reports confirm that non-programmers build Zap workflows with multiple trigger and action steps through an intuitive interface, and Canvas offers visual process mapping that leads into automation. First-party docs never directly describe a no-code, multi-step visual Zap editor, and the 'Visual Builder' docs cover building integrations, not workflows. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of a visual multi-step Zap editor, explicit docs on branching and conditional steps, evidence for complex workflows (one user says simple if-this-then-that workflows break down for complex automation).

support.subject: As an ops user, I can build multi-step workflows in a visual editor without writing code

citations.quote: The fact that it could get done by a non-programmer made the monthly fee very worth paying.
Zapier allows more simultaneous IFs & THENs
Zapier is a little more intuitive interface-wise.
Canvas automatically maps and optimizes your processes to help your team document, refine, and automate with ease.
